source_text: Περὶ ἀναστάσεως πρὸς Σαδδουκαίους. «Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται.» Ἀλληγορητέον ὡς παρὰ τῷ Ἀποστόλῳ περὶ παιδίσκης καὶ ἐλευθέρας· οἱ σωματικῶς τὰ περὶ γάμων ἐκλαμβάνοντες πλανῶνται ὥσπερ οἱ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν βρώματα σωματικὰ προσδοκῶντες. «Θεὸς οὐκ ἔστιν νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων· πάντες γὰρ αὐτῷ ζῶσιν.» Δόξα Χριστῷ. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: On the resurrection against the Sadducees
orientation: Origen is closing the commentary with the Sadducees' question about the resurrection, interpreting Jesus' answer spiritually.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning [the] resurrection to [the] Sadducees. "[You] go astray not knowing the writings nor the power of God; for in the resurrection neither [do they] marry nor [are they] given in marriage." [It is] to be allegorized as by the Apostle concerning [the] maidservant and [the] free woman; the [ones] bodily the [things] concerning marriages taking [are] going astray just as the [ones] after the resurrection foods bodily expecting. "God not is of dead [ones] but of living [ones]; for all to him live." Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: The verbal adjective expresses necessity; rendering as a finite passive keeps the impersonal force without adding a subject.
The adverb modifies how they take the matters concerning marriages; 'bodily' preserves the contrast with allegorical interpretation.
The participle conveys anticipation of future bodily foods; 'expecting' keeps the forward-looking sense.
A doxological formula; the dative of recipient is rendered with 'to' as in standard English doxologies.

bible_refs.note: Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται
Θεὸς οὐκ ἔστιν νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων· πάντες γὰρ αὐτῷ ζῶσιν

pass_b_english: On the resurrection, against the Sadducees. “You are deceived, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God; for in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage” (Matthew 22:29-30). This must be allegorized, as the Apostle does with the slave woman and the free woman (Galatians 4:22-31). Those who take the matters concerning marriages bodily are deceived, just like those who expect bodily foods after the resurrection. “God is not God of the dead but of the living; for all are alive to him” (Matthew 22:32). Glory to Christ. Amen.

last_rejected.why: Active 'you deceive yourselves' or 'you go astray', not passive 'you are deceived'.
last_rejected.ruling: Πλανᾶσθε is deponent middle/passive; 'you are deceived/led astray' is within normal range.

last_rejected.ruling: Ἀλληγορητέον = 'must be allegorized' is rendered correctly; article asymmetry is minor English style.

last_rejected.fix: God is not of the dead but of the living
